summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of kidney transplantation was readmitted within 24 hours of discharge due to recurrent fever and vomiting while on outpatient ertapenem for a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary tract infection. She was transitioned back to IV meropenem and monitored closely. Renal ultrasounds showed stable transplant kidneys with no abscess or obstruction. After 24 hours of being afebrile on meropenem, she was switched back to ertapenem for completion of a 14-day course at home via a midline. Hypertension was identified during admission, and she was started on losartan. She remained afebrile, with stable renal function and transplant medication levels, and was discharged home with visiting nurse support for antibiotic administration and clear instructions on medication resumption, glycemic control, and vaginal estrogen use to reduce future infection risk.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Klebsiella pneumoniae [K. pneumoniae] as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
Family history of disorders of kidney and ureter
